quest.title: The Amethyst Athenaeum
quest.description: There was no other viable option it seemed. The ghoulish fetish carved from the flesh of slain acolytes and used in a, thus far, unknown ritual seemed to have been created by someone who was going well out of their way to deflect any investigations. The mere fact that there existed not one, but two fairly convoluted misdirections spoke of a mind that thought ahead in a highly strategic fashion.

node.instruction: Search for clues within the Athenaeum
node.journal_entry: One book, "Mercia: A Royal Treatise", seemed to have several pages that had nothing to do with the volume pushed in at random intervals. The invading pages however seemed to be from a documentation called The History of the Watchers. That seemed fairly odd in itself.

node.instruction: Search for clues within the Athenaeum
node.journal_entry: Here was a documentation on the History of the Watchers with several pages brutally ripped out!

node.instruction: Search for clues within the Athenaeum
node.journal_entry: A cartographer's journal entitled "Maps of Agon" seemed to have a number of maps squashed back inside as if someone had tried to fold them back in a hurry! Closer inspection revealed a map of a particular little island you had so recently visited. This could be no coincidence!

node.instruction: Search for clues within the Athenaeum
node.journal_entry: A tome entitled "Gods and Avatars" seemed to be missing several volumes out of it's seven book series. This was, perhaps, important.

You approached the Librarian and informed him of your quest as well as the clues you had now discovered. He seemed to listen with some measure of interest, but his ire was only truly sparked when you showed him the torn book and missing volumes. He was aghast and declared, in his own words, "this criminal, the most base creature lacking in any decorum and respect must be found at all costs!"

It seemed you had definitely uncovered a pattern here. Someone had recently been here and researching something fairly suspicious. Plus, with the missing tomes and ripped pages, you had a feeling that the overly bibliophilic Acolyte would surely want to help you.
As an afterthought he also agreed that stopping whatever dark machinations this defiler of books was planning would probably also be good.

Together, you went over the clues again, trying to glean details and possible points of interest. Behrem noted that the pages torn out of the History of Acolytes seemed to be jammed in between pages that spoke of the lineage of the kings of Mercia. Too, he noticed that particular attention seemed to have been given to passages about the immortality of the Acolytes, a gift from the Watcher, and the creation of mortal vessels in the form of avatars for higher beings.

node.instruction: Locate the Amethyst Athenaeum within the Tovarr lands.
node.journal_entry: Upon entering the area around the Athenaeum, it seemed to me that a sense of foreboding seemed to fill you. Was there perhaps a certain dismay clouding your features as you viewed the piles and rows of books around this place of knowledge? Or was it perhaps a look of awe when you realized how much lore might be held here, a part of the land that seemed to be packed to the brim with books and volumes on everything possible?

action.tag: An Add Quest Area to World-Map Action

node.instruction: Search for clues within the Athenaeum
node.journal_entry: The keeper of the books, a perpetually distracted looking Acolyte who was known as Behrem the Aesthetic informed you that you were welcome to look around and use the tomes to help your investigation. He simply asked that you respect the books and take care not to damage any of the precious volumes.

The Shaman bade you make haste to the Amethyst Athenaeum in hopes that you would find answers there. As an afterthought, he also mentioned that, should you need to contact him from afar, you could find Orkish emissaries in every capital city.
Either way, it seemed you had your work cut out for you...

And finally, $[Vendors.q09_quest_acolyte_librarian_Name] also mentioned that all the books of the Athenaeum were enchanted with tracking magics to prevent theft and loss. After several long moments of what I felt was a particularly grim stare from your direction he exclaimed that perhaps that would be a great way to find your culprit!
